{"status": "NO_PLAN", "reasons": ["CS4278 is a must-take course. Its prerequisites are CS3263 or CS3243, MA2001/MA1522/MA1101R/MA1311/MA1508E/MA1513, and EE2012/EE2012A/ST2131/ST2334/MA2116/MA2116T/MA2216, and MA2002/MA1102R/MA1505/MA1507/MA1521/(MA1512 and MA1511). The student has MA1522, ST2334, and MA1521. However, the student has not completed MA2001, MA1101R, MA1311, MA1508E, MA1513, MA2002, MA1102R, MA1505, MA1507, MA1521 (wait, MA1521 is completed), or the EE/ST/MA2116/MA2116T/MA2216 group (student has ST2334, but ST2334 is mutually exclusive with ST2131/MA2116 etc? No, ST2334 is in the list. Wait, ST2334 is in the prereq list for CS4278? Yes: 'EE2012 or EE2012A or ST2131 or ST2334 or MA2116 or MA2116T or MA2216'. Student has ST2334. So that part is met. The student has MA1521. So that part is met. The student has MA1522. But MA1522 is not in the prereq list for CS4278. The list is MA2001 or MA1522 or MA1101R or MA1311 or MA1508E or MA1513. Student has MA1522. So that part is met. So CS4278 prerequisites are met if CS3263 or CS3243 is completed. CS3263 is offered Sem 1 and Sem 2. CS3243 is offered Sem 2. CS4278 is offered Sem 1. So CS4278 can be taken in Sem 1 (Y3S1, Y4S1). CS3263 can be taken in Y3S1. So CS4278 can be taken in Y4S1. But the student must take CS4278. It is not in the 'must take' list? Yes it is: 'I must take CS3282, CS3219, CS4278, CS4246...'. So CS4278 is a must-take. I missed it in the previous plan. CS4278 is 4 MC. It needs CS3263 or CS3243. CS3263 is offered Sem 1. CS3243 is offered Sem 2. If we use CS3263, it can be in Y3S1. Then CS4278 can be in Y4S1. But Y4S1 has CS3268 and CS3281. CS4278 is 4 MC. Y4S1 limit 12. 4+4+4=12. So Y4S1: CS3268, CS3281, CS4278. This works. But wait, CS3281 is NOT offered in Sem 1. CS3281 is offered Sem 2. So CS3281 cannot be in Y4S1 (Sem 7). CS3281 must be in Sem 2 (Y3S2, Y4S2). If CS3281 is in Y3S2, then CS3282 (prereq CS3281) can be in Y4S1 or Y4S2. CS3282 is offered Sem 2. So CS3282 must be in Y3S2 or Y4S2. If CS3281 is Y3S2, CS3282 can be Y4S2. CS3268 is offered Sem 1. So CS3268 can be Y3S1, Y4S1. CS3268 must be after CS4246 (Y3S2). So CS3268 is Y4S1. CS3268 must be before CS3282. So CS3268 (Y4S1) before CS3282 (Y4S2). This works. CS4278 is offered Sem 1. So CS4278 can be Y3S1 or Y4S1. CS4278 prereq CS3263/CS3243. CS3263 offered Sem 1, Sem 2. If CS3263 is Y3S1, CS4278 can be Y4S1. Y4S1: CS3268, CS4278. CS3281 is Y3S2. CS3282 is Y4S2. This seems possible. Let's re-verify CS3281 offering. 'CS3281 Software Engineering for Evolving Production Systems I | 4 MC | offered: Sem 2'. Correct. So CS3281 cannot be in Sem 1. My previous error was putting CS3281 in Sem 7 (Y4S1). CS3281 must be in Sem 2. So Y3S2 or Y4S2. If Y3S2, it takes a slot. Y3S2 has CS4246, CS3219, ES2660. That's 12 MC. Adding CS3281 (4 MC) makes 16 MC. Limit 12. So CS3281 cannot be in Y3S2. So CS3281 must be in Y4S2. But Y4S2 limit is 1 module. CS3282 is also in Y4S2. So CS3281 and CS3282 cannot both be in Y4S2. Can CS3281 be in Y4S2 and CS3282 in Y4S2? No, 1 module limit. Can CS3281 be in Y4S2 and CS3282 in Y4S1? No, CS3282 is offered Sem 2. Y4S1 is Sem 1. So CS3282 cannot be in Y4S1. So CS3282 must be in Y4S2. So CS3281 must be before Y4S2. So CS3281 must be in Y3S2. But Y3S2 is full (12 MC) with CS4246, CS3219, ES2660. Can we move one of them? CS4246 must be in Y3S2. CS3219 and ES2660 can be moved. CS3219 is offered Sem 1, Sem 2. ES2660 is offered Sem 1, Sem 2. If we move CS3219 to Y3S1, Y3S1 has CS3263, CS2102, CS2105 (12 MC). Adding CS3219 (4 MC) makes 16 MC. Limit 12. So CS3219 cannot be in Y3S1. If we move ES2660 to Y3S1, same problem. If we move CS2102 or CS2105? CS2102 and CS2105 are eligible in Y3S1. If we move CS2102 to Y3S2, Y3S2 has CS4246, CS3219, ES2660, CS2102. 16 MC. Too many. If we move CS2105 to Y3S2, same. If we move CS3263? CS3263 is prereq for CS4246 and CS3268. CS3263 must be before Y3S2. So CS3263 must be in Y3S1. So Y3S1 must have CS3263. Y3S1 limit 12. CS3263 is 4 MC. Remaining 8 MC. CS2102 (4), CS2105 (4). Total 12. So Y3S1 is full with CS3263, CS2102, CS2105. Y3S2 must have CS4246 (4 MC). Remaining 8 MC. CS3281 (4 MC) must be in Y3S2 (since Y4S2 is full with CS3282 and 1 module limit). So Y3S2 has CS4246, CS3281. Remaining 4 MC. CS3219 (4 MC) or ES2660 (4 MC). We need to take both. So one must be in Y4S1. Y4S1 has CS3268 (4 MC). Remaining 8 MC. CS3219 (4 MC) and ES2660 (4 MC). Total 12 MC. So Y4S1: CS3268, CS3219, ES2660. Y4S2: CS3282. This works. CS3281 is in Y3S2 (Sem 2). CS3282 is in Y4S2 (Sem 2). CS3268 is in Y4S1 (Sem 1). CS3268 before CS3282. OK. CS4246 in Y3S2. OK. CS4278? I forgot CS4278 again. CS4278 is a must-take. CS4278 is offered Sem 1. Prereq CS3263/CS3243. CS3263 is in Y3S1. So CS4278 can be in Y4S1. Y4S1 has CS3268, CS3219, ES2660. Total 12 MC. Adding CS4278 (4 MC) makes 16 MC. Limit 12. So CS4278 cannot be in Y4S1. Can CS4278 be in Y3S1? Y3S1 is full. Can CS4278 be in Y3S2? No, offered Sem 1. Can CS4278 be in Y4S1? No, full. Can CS4278 be in Y4S2? No, offered Sem 1. So CS4278 cannot be scheduled. Therefore, NO_PLAN.
